extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of aesthetics (artists, writers, philosophers)
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical guidance on evaluating and producing beauty of form, focusing on the relations among dignity, grace, love/esteem, and the proper limits of taste and imagination in moral action, artistic expression, and the communication of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral goodness requires participation of inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: An action is morally good only as far as inclination has taken part in it; when inclination protests rather than concurs, the action lacks 'moral beauty' though it may have moral grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes 'moral beauty' (where inclination cooperates with duty) from moral grandeur (where reason represses inclination). Use this to evaluate moral tone in characters/acts: purely dutiful acts without felt inclination lack moral beauty even if morally right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral grandeur arises from preponderant authority of reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions in which reason rules sensitiveness—where the will represses instincts and acts exclusively from reason—may lack moral beauty but possess moral grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when representing heroic or austere characters: grandeur is the expression of authority over sensuous nature and can be valued distinct from warmth or grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity defined as rule over instincts by moral force
rubrics_metrics.description: Dignity is the emancipation of mind expressed phenomenally when the will resists and masters involuntary movements and instincts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phenomenal signs: calmness under suffering, serenity of brow and look despite involuntary signs of affection. Dignity is required where instinct must be restrained; but is ridiculous where there is nothing to resist. Degrees include nobleness (toward grace) and haughtiness (toward fear); highest form = majesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace as liberty of voluntary movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grace is the mind governing sensuous nature with liberal government—voluntary movements flow freely because sensuous nature obeys willingly; it is shown in conduct and in the ease of voluntary expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grace is needed where actions fall within human nature and no struggle is required. It conciliates and attracts (kindliness/love). Types: calming grace (promotes repose) and attractive grace (stimulates imagination). Avoid affected grace (coquetry, artificiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate pairing of dignity and grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Grace and dignity do not exclude each other; ideally they co-exist—grace accredits dignity, dignity gives value to grace—yielding the ideal of human beauty when united.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In characterization and style, seek a balance: grace attests feeling and harmony, dignity attests independent moral force. Their union (smile, serene look) produces attraction and repulsion appropriate to sublime human beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of false/affected grace and dignity (avoid affectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation that copies external signs without the underlying moral state yields affectation: affected grace becomes coquetry; affected dignity becomes stiff solemnity or false gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect via exaggeration and unnatural restraint: affected grace shows studied, tremulous gestures; affected dignity over-controls voluntary movements and hides nature. Authenticity requires imitating the moral state, not surface mannerisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to prefer dignity over grace (and vice versa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dignity is required when a duty demands going beyond human instinct (sacrifice, suffering); grace is demanded where actions are within the harmony of human nature and no struggle is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate situations/characters: in painful sacrifices, visible struggle and dignity confirm the possibility of victory and humanity; in everyday virtuous acts, grace is preferable to display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful exterior expression depends on interior moral state
rubrics_metrics.description: Exterior calmness with inward struggle is the indirect representation of moral force; the visible opposition between involuntary suffering and voluntary serenity indicates autonomy of the will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasts in physical expression (e.g., stifled voice vs serene brow) to signify moral force. Beware of interpreting mere hardness or calculated restraint as dignity; grace combined with dignity vouches for sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish esteem, love, and desire as evaluative responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Esteem inclines toward the object (object = reason); love approaches with inclination (object sensuous; subject moral); desire precipitately seizes the object (both object and subject sensuous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True beauty/grace should awaken kindliness or contentment, not mere desire; true greatness should not cause fear. If fear or desire predominates, either the object or the spectator's conscience/taste is defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Majesty and ravishing charm as extremes (use cautiously)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extremes of dignity/grace: ravishing charm (utmost grace) fuses Ego with object and can overwhelm liberty; majesty (utmost dignity) imposes a law and prostrates the mind—belongs to holiness rather than mere power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve these extremes for subjects/characters that genuinely embody holiness or ecstatic union; power alone does not confer majesty. Overuse or inappropriate application leads to alienation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art may legitimately use solemnity to prepare for impression
rubrics_metrics.description: A properly employed solemnity in art tunes the mind to receive a great impression; art can make use of solemnity as a preparatory device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solemn style can be an acceptable formal device when the goal is to produce a strong, important reception—distinguish this from merely affected gravity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on the use of beauty of form in knowledge and duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste should harmonize sensuous and spiritual powers, but must not extend into domains where we must act as pure creatures of reason—knowledge and moral duty require exclusion of sensuous influence from content and decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the objective is strict knowledge or moral action, minimize ornamental beauty. For scientific/propositional exposition, the mode of presentation must conform to laws of thought; ornament may aid attention but must not disrupt logical necessity or the chain of reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination must be subordinated to the understanding for strict conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination thrives on individual, sensuous representations and freedom in combinations; understanding demands abstract, necessary conceptual sequences—mixing imagination's particulars into chains of abstraction undermines logical necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In argumentative or rigorous expository writing, avoid inserting individualized illustrative images that imply accidental/time-bound particulars; favor clear conceptual sequencing. Reserve imaginative particulars for popular exposition or when the aim is to arouse receptivity rather than strict conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate moderation of ornament when communicating truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Graceful embodiment of conceptions can place the reader in a favorable attitude to receive truth, but the substance must itself commend to the understanding; beauty of form should not replace strictness of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use elegance of form sparingly to open receptivity (especially for popular audiences), but ensure that the substance stands on its own. Excessive ornamentation may defeat the end of convincing scientifically-minded readers.
